Schaeffler opens Taicang factory with six humanoids assembling robot components

Five workstations connect joint-module manufacturing with training and a digital twin across approximately 7,500 square meters.

Humanoids Daily ↗20 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

A component-manufacturing facility

Schaeffler opened its humanoid robotics lighthouse factory in Taicang, China, on October 20. Approximately 7,500 square meters combine assembly, training and data collection, digital twins and a data center. The company describes the opening as the start of mass production of joint modules, including linear and rotary actuators.

Six robots across five stations

Six humanoids prepare and sort parts, assemble them, inspect, label and package them across five stations. The scope is key components rather than complete humanoid assembly. Sensors track accuracy, task time, energy and equipment condition so line changes can be tested digitally before physical implementation.

Training linked to industrial conditions

Training draws on tasks across roughly 100 Schaeffler plants, including inspection, transport and line-side replenishment, with access for customers and partners. The company reports about €400 million in global incoming humanoid orders, not recognized revenue. Production rate and human-intervention requirements remain undisclosed.
